text.en: Nacho, an Aegirian islander, proficient in hydrographic surveying and geographic modeling. After the port salvage project concluded, he joined Rhodes Island through Clementia's recommendation, stationed in Iberia as a cooperative operator to assist Rhodes Island with hydrological observation, climate monitoring, and other work in the coastal areas of Iberia.
text.zh: 纳乔，阿戈尔岛民，精通水文测绘及地理建模。港都打捞工程结束后，经由克莱门莎引荐加入罗德岛，作为合作干员常驻伊比利亚，协助罗德岛进行伊比利亚沿海地区的水文观测与气候监测等工作。

text.en:
Imaging tests show clear organ outlines and no abnormal shadows in this Operator. No abnormalities were detected in the circulatory system's Originium particle tests, showing no signs of Oripathy infection. The Operator is currently confirmed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Lasswell shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12 u/L
Operator Lasswell cooperated with us to complete the basic medical check-up items, but items related to his special conditions (burns, severed limbs) were all things he asked the Doctor to inspect.
Along with sending over those test results, the Doctor also brought a letter from Lasswell. In the letter, he constantly apologizes, trying to explain that asking the Doctor to check those items wasn't directed at the Medical Department, but simply because the Doctor makes him feel slightly more at ease—though that wasn't our fault, it was his own problem...
How are we supposed to tell him that overthinking things all the time is also bad for his health?
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员旅骨没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员旅骨配合我们完成了基本的体检项目，但与他的特殊状况（烧伤、断肢）相关的项目，都是他拜托博士进行检查的。
博士送来那些检查结果的同时，也捎来了旅骨的一封信。在信里，他不断地道歉，试图说明他拜托博士检查那些项目并不是在针对医疗部，只是因为博士能让他稍稍安心些，但那也不是我们的错，是他自己的问题……
我们该怎么和他说，总是想这么多也很不利于身体健康？

text.en:
"So, is this considered practice makes perfect?"
When the curious HR operator asked this question, Nacho's spherical detection device was scanning a corridor on Rhodes Island, where a young patient's flying toy had gone missing nearby. That piece of equipment was originally used in Iberia to sense maritime climate in addition to detecting seabed structures. On the fifth day after Nacho arrived at Rhodes Island, he stood outside the Engineering Department and made a modification request to the first Engineering Department operator who took the initiative to greet him. When the Engineering Department operator asked why, he sheepishly produced three "Lost Property Retrieval Notice Letters"—now this device could scan the basic spatial conditions of any building and environment, and Nacho naturally became a volunteer at the Lost and Found.
"I don't know why I lose so many things in a day either; it wouldn't do to cause trouble for the operators at the Lost and Found..." Nacho squatted down and placed the scanning panel in front of the young patient. The child poked the glowing spot—her toy was stuck in the ventilation duct. Nacho lay flat on the floor by the wall and reached in to grab it.
Nacho is undoubtedly a likable person. Although he looks like a cold current hovering over the Iberian sea and has a severed arm, he is very happy to help out. However, whenever he encounters troubles he needs to deal with, he isn't very good at asking others for help. After older operators go on missions with him, they turn into his "guardians" in a sense.
"Oh!"
"Oh! You got little Raina's toy?"
"I might know why I lose so many things."
"Why?"
"When working at the Rea-Iberia Salvage Center, technicians would wear diving suits when going underwater. Even if things were lost, they were only lost inside the diving suit, and you just had to dump them out. That way most personal items wouldn't get lost. However, I always felt that working this way was too inefficient, so I would stick my prosthetic limb out of the diving suit and operate directly in the seawater, and as a result I would lose bolts, haha..."
"Haha?"
"And speaking of the prosthetic limb, I know how to get the toy back now. Could I ask you to use the weather orb to distract little Raina's attention?"
Nacho unbuckled the clasp of his prosthetic limb. The detached arm operated a few times under Nacho's remote control and climbed into the duct like a pod-limbed organism to retrieve the toy. Until it was reattached to Nacho, the HR operator's look of horror had not faded.
"Sorry, I didn't think it would scare you too?"
"...I suppose I understand why you have so many 'guardians'; now I really want to join them. Even if it's just a prosthetic, attaching and detaching it puts a burden on your body all the same. Please don't do that so casually again."
"The parts of this prosthetic limb once helped Supervisor Clementia recover Rea-Iberia, making me an 'hero' in the eyes of some Iberians. This title makes me feel very, very unsettled. I'd rather use it to retrieve a flying toy and be little Raina's 'hero'."
"..."
"Hm? Why aren't you saying anything?"
"..."
"I shouldn't talk either? Just accept your hug? O-Okay..."
text.zh:
“所以，这算是熟能生巧？”
好奇的人事干员提问时，纳乔的球形探测装置正在扫描罗德岛的一处通道，一位小患者的飞行玩具在这附近不见了。那件设备在伊比利亚原本用于感知海上气候外加探测海床结构。纳乔来到罗德岛的第五天，他站在工程部外，向第一位主动跟他打招呼的工程部干员提出了改造需求。当工程部干员询问原因时，他不好意思地拿出了三封“遗失物取回提示函”——现在这件装置已经可以扫描任何建筑和环境的基础空间状况，纳乔也自然成为了失物招领处的志愿者。
“我也不知道为什么自己一天会丢那么多东西，给失物招领处的干员添麻烦可不好……”纳乔蹲下来，把扫描面板放到小患者面前。孩子戳了戳发光的地方——她的玩具卡在了通风管道里。纳乔趴在墙边的地上伸手去够。
纳乔毫无疑问是个招人喜欢的人。尽管他看上去像是伊比利亚海上盘旋的冷空气，还有一只断臂，但他非常乐意帮忙。不过，每当他遇到自己需要处理的麻烦时，又不太擅长向他人求助。有些年长的干员与他一同出过任务之后，就会变成他某种意义上的“监护者”。
“哦！”
“哦！你拿到小雷娜的玩具了？”
“我可能知道我为什么会丢那么多东西了。”
“为什么？”
“在雷亚-伊比利亚打捞中心工作的时候，技术工们下水都会穿潜水服，即使东西丢了也只是丢在潜水服里，把它们倒出来就好了。这样一来大部分个人物品都不会弄丢。不过，我总觉得这样工作的效率太低，就把义肢伸出潜水服，直接在海水中进行作业，结果就弄丢了螺栓，哈哈……”
“哈哈？”
“以及，说到义肢，我知道怎么拿回玩具了，可以请你用气象球引开小雷娜的注意力吗？”
纳乔解开了义肢的卡扣，脱离主人的手臂在纳乔的远程操作下活动了几下，像只星荚外生物一样“七手八脚”地爬进管道取出了玩具。直到它被装回纳乔身上，人事干员惊恐的神色还未褪去。
“抱歉，我没想到也会吓到你？”
“……我算是知道你为什么会有那么多‘监护者’了，现在我也很想加入他们。尽管只是义肢，但装卸它对你的身体同样有负担，请不要再轻易这么做了。”
“这只义肢的零件曾帮克莱门莎监事找回了雷亚-伊比利亚，让我成为了一些伊比利亚人眼中的‘英雄’。这个称呼让我非常非常不踏实。我更想用它找回一件飞行玩具，做小雷娜的‘英雄’。”
“……”
“嗯？你怎么不说话了？”
“……”
“我也不要说话？接受你的拥抱就好？好、好的……”

text.en:
[Rhodes Island Internal Forum Public Board: A Late Apology]
I deeply repent.
When I went to the Engineering Department for a meeting last month, I saw a young man cutting sugarcane into a flowerpot. I thought the Rhodes Island office environment improvement group was working on some new modification, so I casually chatted with this sugarcane farmer for a bit. He's a bit introverted, quite cute, and told me a lot of popular science about sugarcane seedlings and Iberia's sandy loam. Good thing he was keeping me company, otherwise I wouldn't have known what to say when I first met Mr. Nacho, the technical lead for Port Celen's hydrographic surveying; sugarcane might actually be a topic. Well, I suppose reading up to this point, some people already know what kind of mistake I made. But last month, foolish old me didn't realize he was Mr. Nacho until I watched the "sugarcane farmer" finish moving five bags of sandy loam himself, sat down panting in front of me, and took out the engineering plan...

Reply: Hahaha, are engineering majors really all that versatile?
Reply: Stop laughing, I already feel guilty enough.
Reply: Don't take it too harsh, people from every department love running to the Engineering Department, mistaking people is completely normal. Yesterday I waited forever for my counterpart engineer in Engineering, only to see the curly-haired guy who serves food in the cafeteria enter the office; maybe he went to harvest sugarcane, haha.
Reply: Curly-haired guy... Is he an Aegirian with a prosthetic right arm?
Reply: Yeah. Hey, how do you know?
Reply: ...

In just one week, the replies under the apology post for mistaking Nacho grew more and more numerous. People guessed the identity of this Operator one after another, the discussion completely deviating from the poster's original intent, and the final conclusion was—Nacho is a humanoid weapon secretly researched in Columbia, a single-armed iron-armed man. This matter only came to an end when Nacho himself saw the post, apologized to the poster, and almost even made his resume public.
Before joining Rhodes Island, Nacho had worked no less than twenty different jobs: sugarcane farmer, sugar compounder, net weaver, locksmith, acolyte... There would be longer or shorter gaps between each job. When we asked Nacho afterwards, we learned that most of those "gaps" were because he was summoned by the Inquisition regarding matters concerning his islander compatriots, or because he had to seek further treatment due to worsening phantom pain in his severed limb. Although Iberia has stepped onto the path of reform, one can guess that many of Nacho's previous job changes might have been related to the marginalization of Iberian commoners. To this, Nacho's response was simple: apart from force majeure, the most important reason he changed jobs frequently was to let Iberians see that he is also an ordinary Iberian and that he works for Iberia as well. Some islander compatriots—even his once-best friend—believed that this desire for recognition was merely pandering to Iberians and would not bring true equality to islanders. But in Nacho's view, setting aside all complex considerations and the instigation of lingering grievances, his diverse work experience taught him how to live well in Iberia, especially after his grandmother Rufina passed away.
text.zh:
【罗德岛内部论坛公共版面：迟来的道歉】
我深刻忏悔。
上个月去工程部开会时，看到有个年轻人正在往花盆里扦插甘蔗。我以为罗德岛的办公室环境改善小组又在进行什么新的改良，就随口跟这个甘蔗农聊了两句。他有点内向，挺可爱的，跟我说了很多关于甘蔗苗和伊比利亚沙壤土之类的科普。还好有他作伴，不然我根本不知道初见港都的水文测绘技术负责人纳乔先生的时候应该说些什么，甘蔗可能是个话题。嗯，我想读到这里，有些人已经知道我犯了什么样的错误。但上个月，愚蠢的我直到看着“甘蔗农”亲自搬完五袋沙壤土，在我面前喘着气坐下，拿出工程计划书的时候，我才知道他就是纳乔先生……

回复：哈哈哈学工程的都那么多才多艺吗？
回复：别笑了，我已经很内疚了。
回复：别太在意，哪个部门的人都喜欢往工程部跑，认错很正常。昨天我去工程部等对接的工程师，等了半天只看到食堂给我打饭的卷发小哥进了办公室，说不定他就是去收甘蔗的哈哈。
回复：卷发小哥……他是不是阿戈尔人，右臂是义肢？
回复：对啊。欸，你怎么知道？
回复：……

短短一个星期，将纳乔认错的道歉帖下的回复越来越多。人们纷纷揣测这名干员的身份，讨论完全偏离了发帖人的初衷，最后的结论是——纳乔是哥伦比亚秘密研究的人形武器，单手铁臂人。此事直到纳乔本人看到帖子，跟发帖人致歉，甚至差点公开自己的简历，才得以收场。
在入职罗德岛之前，纳乔曾做过不下二十种不同的工作：甘蔗农、配糖员、织网工、锁匠、辅祭……每份工作之间都会有或长或短的间隔，询问纳乔之后我们得知，那些“间隔”大多是他因为岛民同胞的事情配合审判庭传唤，或是因为断肢的幻痛加剧不得不寻求进一步治疗。尽管伊比利亚已踏上变革的道路，但可以猜测，在此之前纳乔许多次职业的变更或许与伊比利亚平民的排挤有关。对此，纳乔的回应很简单，除了不可抗力，他频繁换工作，最重要的原因是为了让伊比利亚人看到，他也是一名普通的伊比利亚人，他也在为伊比利亚工作。有些岛民同胞——甚至他曾经最好的朋友都认为，这种渴望获得认可的行为只是在讨好伊比利亚人，不会为岛民带来真正的平等。但在纳乔看来，抛开一切复杂的考量和积怨的煽动，他多样的工作经历教会了他如何在伊比利亚好好活下去，尤其是在奶奶鲁菲纳过世之后。

text.en:
We almost threw hands.
When we learned that Rufina's grandson was safe and sound and that she was willing to raise him, we were actually all very happy. During those three months when she was agonizing over not knowing what to name him, we all helped think of names. Yet no one expected that what she ultimately decided on was actually an Iberian name.
It's not that islanders can't have Iberian names; too many of our compatriots have forgotten our ancestors' naming rules and had to switch to Iberian names instead—there's nothing to that. But Rufina? She was the one person who couldn't possibly do such a thing.
When all is said and done, the reason we gathered here, discussing how to resist and how to struggle, was all because of Rufina. If not for her, we probably would have just stood by and watched compatriots get stabbed, burned, and nailed to lamp posts one after another.
Rufina never accepted this reality. The islanders had made contributions to Iberia, and the islanders had not brought disaster to Iberia—she spent the latter half of her life trying to prove these things. She told every one of us to remember everything about Aegir, because if we don't remember, no one else ever will either.
And then, she gave her own grandson a quintessential Iberian name?
Those of us who were the most radical even suspected that she had betrayed us. That night, no matter how people reproached her, Rufina said nothing. In the end, everyone's voices grew hoarse from arguing, and she dropped a single sentence:
"Whatever I am trying to prove, it has nothing to do with that child."
After that, she never took action with us again.
——An islander who once participated in sabotage operations

"Name?"
"Nacho."
"Surname?"
"Uh... García López."
"Is the paternal surname first or the maternal surname first?"
"Uh, no. My parents both had Aegirian names, and my first and last names were both made up out of thin air by my grandmother. They're the most common and ordinary ones, to make me look more like an Iberian..."
"Understood. Then would you like to change the registered name? We can handle that.
"N-No need. The current name is fine, I like it very much. Although it actually can't change anyone's view of me at all, but... the name itself is great.
"All right.
"But, if possible... I'd still prefer it if the files didn't have a surname, and just said 'Nacho'. That way, it's better for everyone..."
"Better for everyone? Why?"
——HR Information Registration Office, a dialogue

What Nacho borrows the most here is always technical manuals, and sometimes he borrows novels too. But recently, he has been borrowing fewer and fewer novels and more and more scripts.
Looking at the books he returns, it isn't hard to understand why. For all the novels he reads, although he tries very hard to smooth out the pages, you can still tell that the first few dozen pages are much fluffier than the back; he must have flipped through the front parts over and over again. But in the case of scripts, the traces of repeated thumbing are limited strictly to the cast list right at the front.
I'm guessing Nacho must be someone very bad at remembering names. For novels, he has to flip back to see who is who after reading two pages; by contrast, the advantage of a script is that all the characters' names are neatly listed right at the very front.
Ha, if everyone's name in a book were as short and easy to remember as "Nacho," he would definitely be able to read much more easily.
——Librarian of the Rhodes Island Library
text.zh:
我们差点就动手了。
知道鲁菲纳的孙子平安无事，她也愿意抚养他的时候，我们其实都很高兴。她纠结着不知道该给他起什么名字的那三个月里，我们也都帮忙想了。可谁也没料到，最后她决定的，居然是个伊比利亚名字。
不是说岛民不能起伊比利亚名字，我们有太多同胞都忘了祖辈的命名规则，只好改用伊比利亚名字，这都没什么。但鲁菲纳？唯独她不可能这么做。
说到底，我们会聚在这里，商量着怎么反抗、怎么挣扎，都是因为鲁菲纳。如果不是她，我们大概就只会眼睁睁看着一个又一个的同胞被捅死、被烧死、被钉上灯柱。
鲁菲纳从来都不接受这样的现实。岛民为伊比利亚做过贡献，岛民没有给伊比利亚带来灾难——她后半辈子都在试图证明这些。她叫我们每个人记住有关阿戈尔的一切，因为如果我们不记得，就再也不会有人记得了。
然后，她给自己的孙子起了个地地道道的伊比利亚名字？
我们之中最激进的那几个年轻人，甚至怀疑她是背叛了我们。那一晚上，不论被人怎么指责，鲁菲纳都不说话。到最后，所有人都吵哑了嗓子，她才撂下一句话：
“我想证明什么，都和那个孩子没关系。”
那之后，她再没和我们一起行动过。
——曾参与过破坏行动的一位岛民

“名字？”
“纳乔。”
“姓氏？”
“呃……加西亚·洛佩兹。”
“父姓在前还是母姓在前？”
“呃，不是。我父母都是阿戈尔名字，我的名字和姓氏都是奶奶凭空起的，都是最普通最常见的，为了让我更像个伊比利亚人……”
“明白了。那你希望更改登记的名字吗？我们可以处理。”
“不、不用。现在的名字就好，我很喜欢。虽然其实根本改变不了任何人对我的看法，但……名字本身很好。”
“好的。”
“但，如果可以的话……我还是希望档案上不要姓氏，只写‘纳乔’就好。这样的话，对大家都好……”
“对大家都好？为什么？”
——人事部信息登记处，一段对话

纳乔在这里借得最多的永远是技术手册，有时候也会借小说。但最近，他小说借得越来越少，剧本借得越来越多了。
看他还回来的书，就不难理解为什么。他读过的所有小说，虽然他很努力地试图把书页捋平了，但还是看得出前几十页比后面要蓬松得多，他大概是反反复复地翻阅了前面的部分。但如果是剧本，反复翻阅的痕迹就仅限于最前面的人物表。
我猜，纳乔一定是个很不擅长记名字的人。小说的话，看两页就得翻回去找谁是谁，相比之下，剧本的好处就是所有人物的名字都整整齐齐地列在了最前面。
哈，如果书里每个人的名字都像“纳乔”那么短、那么好记，他肯定能读得更轻松些。
——罗德岛图书室的管理员

text.en:
[Unofficial Records of the Rhodes Island Rhea-Iberia Office]
Three mornings ago, when I saw the leader of the islander radical movement—who was wanted by the Inquisition—walk out of Nacho's room, I ought to have worried about Nacho Garcia Lopez's personal safety first, but honestly, the first thought that popped into my head was how the cooperation between Rhodes Island and the Inquisition was going to end.
I have read the report submitted to Rhodes Island by Operator Clementia, which meticulously records a series of events encountered during the port salvaging process, and also mentions Nacho's contribution to the salvaging and the retrieval of Rhea-Iberia's central district. I saw the city that Nacho named "Our Iberia" on the navigational charts being rebuilt, and I saw that roadside shops no longer distinguish between islanders and Iberians, but that doesn't mean the islander issue has been completely resolved in Iberia. Even in the port, even after witnessing the scene of islanders and Iberians salvaging together with my own eyes, there are still people choosing to fight, which makes me uneasy.
So I lost my composure, angrily questioning Nacho whether he violated Rhodes Island's code of conduct and suspecting him of colluding with radicals. But he simply waited for me to vent, and then told me everything about their late-night conversation, word for word.
For an entire night, they didn't say a single word about the port or the situation in Iberia. They simply shared memories. Both of them had lost several family members, several friends, lost jobs that could have allowed them to live steady lives, had once learned to pilot a ship, and then were forbidden from doing so. They talked about whose family member the glowing object on the flag signal tower in the port's central district might have come from, and also talked about how the seaweed wine here differed from other places in Iberia.
I don't understand why these topics could keep them talking for a whole night. No, actually, I do understand. As an Aegirian also born in Iberia, I know deeply that opportunities to talk to others on equal terms are not many, which is why I left my hometown early to come to Rhodes Island. When I learned that an islander used a bolt left behind by a family member to find Iberia's once most prosperous capital, I was quite astonished. What astonished me was not how much luck and effort this step required, but that, as a marginalized individual, Nacho was actually willing to do so.
Nacho told me that the radical who found him did indeed want to ask him for help, but he only promised that he wouldn't tell the Inquisition about their whereabouts and promised nothing else. No disgust, no fear, no worry, none of the emotions I felt when I left Iberia or heard that radicals had come to the office. Nacho calmly told me that he would never bring the islander problems to Rhodes Island, because protecting the islanders is his choice, while joining Rhodes Island is another unrelated choice of his.
He saw my frustration and guilt, and accompanied me by the seaside for a long time. Before leaving, he used his prosthetic limb to awkwardly pat my hand and told me I had worked hard.
text.zh:
【罗德岛驻雷亚-伊比利亚办事处非正式记录】
三天前的清晨，当我看到被审判庭通缉的岛民激进运动领头人从纳乔房间里走出来的时候，我应当首先担心纳乔·加西亚·洛佩兹的人身安全，但诚实地说，我脑中第一个出现的念头是罗德岛与审判庭的合作要如何收场。
我看过干员克莱门莎向罗德岛提交的报告，上面详实记录了港都打捞过程中遇到的一系列事件，也提到了纳乔为打捞以及寻回雷亚-伊比利亚中心城区做出的贡献。我看到这座在海图上被纳乔命名为“我们的伊比利亚”的城市正在重建，也看到沿街的商铺不再将岛民和伊比利亚人区别对待，但这不代表岛民问题已经在伊比利亚得到了彻底解决。哪怕在港都，哪怕亲眼目睹了岛民和伊比利亚人共同打捞的场景，依旧有人选择斗争，这令我不安。
所以我失态了，我愤怒地质问纳乔是否违背了罗德岛的行事准则，怀疑他与激进分子勾结。但他只是等我宣泄完，然后一五一十说出了他们夜谈的所有内容。
一个晚上，他们没有说一句有关港都和伊比利亚局势的话。他们只是在分享回忆。他们都失去了几位亲人，几位朋友，丢掉过好几份可能让他们踏踏实实活下去的工作，曾学过驾船，又被禁止驾船。他们聊港都中心城区旗语塔上发光的物件可能是出自哪位同胞的亲族之手，也聊这里的海藻酒跟伊比利亚其他地方的有什么不同。
我不明白为什么这些话题能让他们聊一个晚上，不，其实我明白。身为一个同样生于伊比利亚的阿戈尔人，我深知跟别人平等交谈的机会并不多，这也是我早早离开家乡来到罗德岛的原因。当我得知有一个岛民用一枚亲人留下的螺栓找到了伊比利亚曾经最繁荣的都城，我十分诧异，我诧异的并非是实现这一步需要多少运气和努力，而是作为被排挤过的一员，纳乔竟然真的愿意这样做。
纳乔告诉我，那个找到他的激进分子确实想向他寻求帮助，但他只是允诺自己不会告诉审判庭他们的消息，除此之外没有答应任何事。没有厌恶，没有恐惧，没有担忧，没有我离开伊比利亚时或听说激进分子来过办事处时的任何情绪，纳乔平静地告诉我，他永远不会把岛民的问题带来罗德岛，因为保护岛民是他的选择，加入罗德岛则是他的另一个无关的选择。
他看出我的沮丧和愧疚，陪我在海边坐了很久，离开前他用义肢不太习惯地拍了拍我的手，对我说辛苦了。

text.en:
Nacho's arm condition is concerning.
After promotion, his sense of responsibility seems even stronger. Nacho actively participates in various affairs between Rhodes Island and Iberia, and hydrographic surveying already puts a burden on his prosthetic limb. Now the number of times he comes to you for prosthetic limb maintenance is increasing...*
"Is it okay to slowly shoulder the responsibilities of new work at my own pace? But—"
"No, no, no, I'm not worried that Rhodes Island won't issue extra pay, nor am I worried about the decline in lubricating oil quality. I'm only working overtime because—uh, I'm only working overtime because..."
"Even if my pay increases, the things I can do and have to do also increase, but the time we spend together is still just this one hour of prosthetic limb maintenance every month, isn't it?"
"If working overtime can increase our maintenance time... Ow, please don't knock on my head..."
"What else do you want to do besides maintenance? Together with me?!"
"I-I haven't thought about it yet... I'll think of something very soon."
text.zh:
纳乔手臂的状况令人担忧。
晋升之后，他的责任感似乎更强了。纳乔主动参与罗德岛和伊比利亚的各项事务，水文测绘本就会为他的义肢带来负担，如今他找你养护义肢的次数越来越多……
“按照我自己的步调，慢慢担起新工作的责任也可以？可——”
“不不不，我不是担心罗德岛不会发放额外的报酬，也不是担心润滑油的品质下降，我加班只是为了——呃，我加班只是因为……”
“就算我的报酬增加了，能做的事、要做的事也变多了，可我们相处的时间依旧只有每个月养护义肢的这一个小时，不是吗？”
“如果加班能增加养护的时间……嘶，请不要敲我的脑袋啊……”
“养护以外还想做什么？我们一起吗？！”
“我、我还没想过……我会很快想出来的。”
